Correct by holding the Code text and recording it as a later event (or explaining why it does not affect the order).

OFR catalog note for EO 11231 (terminal date March 28, 1973)
reasoning: Identity (30 FR 8665, signed 1965-07-08, Johnson), inventory, quotes, the two amendments (EO 11382 sec. 13 item (9), 1967-11-28; EO 13286 sec. 66, effective 2003-03-01) and their dates are correct, and the claim addresses the OFR note that the Secretary of Defense set the terminal date as March 28, 1973 (DoD Instruction 1348.15 memo of 1973-01-26), reasonably treating it as closing the qualifying-service window under section 1's own terms rather than ending the award command. The substantive outcome is defensible. But the rationale says the Code search found no hit for this order, while the packet's own machine search records one hit, the 6 U.S.C. 111 note listing 'Sec. 66. [Amended Ex. Ord. No. 11231.]'. The rule requires searches to be honestly and accurately described; the statement is wrong and must be corrected (the hit should be reported as corroboration of the EO 13286 amendment).
